or (b) harasses, harms, injures or endangers the aggrieved person with a view to coerce her or any other person r to marry any person or to perform any task or undertake any act which such person is not legally required to perform or take; or (c) causes the aggrieved person to leave her shared household against her will by a process of persuasion, threat, coercion or any other means; or (d) discontinues marital access; or (e) disposes of or gives away any ancestral property or any property owned by the aggrieved person or the shared household without the consent of the aggrieved person; or (f) abets or convinces any other person or dowry; or (g) attempts to threaten any person against the aggrieved person or any person who intends to give evidence on behalf of the aggrieved person in any proceeding under this Act; or (h) places physical or mental harassment for the purpose of coercing the aggrieved person or any person related to her by blood, adoption or marriage to meet any unlawful demand for any property or valuable security or anything of a valuable nature; or (i) commits, or causes the commission of, or attempts to commit any act by doing any act mentioned in clause (a) or clause (b) or clause (c) or clause (d) or clause (e) or clause (f) or clause (g) or clause (h) or clause (i) of sub-section (2) of section 3 shall be deemed to have committed an offence under this Act: Provided that a police officer, not below the rank of an inspector, shall investigate and forward the case to the Magistrate of the first class having jurisdiction, and no procedure under the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974) shall apply to the investigation.

CHAPTER III
POWER AND FUNCTIONS OF THE RECTOR, VISITOR AND CHANCELLOR

Rector of the University:

The Governor of the state of Jharkhand shall be the Rector of the university.

Visitor of the University:

The Chief Justice of India shall be the Visitor of the University

(ii) The Vice-Chancellor shall be appointed by the Chancellor in the manner hereinafter provided.

(3) The Vice-Chancellor may, if he is of the opinion that it is expedient so to do, give such directions as he may think fit to any college, institution or other body of higher education as to the manner in which the duties assigned to such college, institution or body under this Act are to be performed.

Notice to quit.-- (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, no landlord shall evict any tenant from any land or building unless he has served on the tenant a notice in writing to quit such land or building. (3) The notice shall specify the date on which the tenant shall quit the land or building. Such date shall not be less than three months from the date of service of the notice. The State of Jharkhand has established the Jharkhand Education Tribunal for the settlement of disputes and adjudication of cases relating to teachers and other employees in the education department of the State of Jharkhand. The Tribunal shall consist of a Chairperson and such number of Members as the State Government may, by notification, appoint. The Chairperson and each Member shall be appointed by the State Government from amongst persons who have been, for at least ten years, members of the Bar, or have been, for at least ten years, in the service of the State or of the Central Government in the post of a Gazetted Officer not below the rank of a Deputy Secretary to the Government. The salary and allowances payable to and the other terms and conditions of service of the Chairperson and Members shall be such as may be prescribed by the State Government. The Tribunal shall have jurisdiction to entertain and dispose of the following cases: (a) a dispute relating to the pay, service conditions, including the determination of seniority, pension and other retirement benefits, or any other matter, relating to a teacher or other employee in the education department of the State of Jharkhand; (b) a dispute relating to the pay, service conditions, including the determination of seniority, pension and other retirement benefits, or any other matter, relating to a teacher or other employee in a local body or an educational institution, who is not a Government employee, but is receiving financial assistance from the State Government or the Government of India, as the case may be; (c) a dispute relating to the pay, service conditions, including the determination of seniority, pension and other retirement benefits, or any other matter, relating to a teacher or other employee in a local body or an educational institution, which is receiving financial assistance from the State Government or the Government of India, as the case may be. The Tribunal shall have jurisdiction to entertain and dispose of an application under this Act only if the amount or the value of the subject matter of the dispute involved in the application is more than fifty thousand rupees. (c) take certified samples of any material.

(g) make a request for the information in any of the languages.

(h) obtain information relating to any public authority.

(i) obtain information from any source.

(j) obtain information in a reasonable time.

(k) obtain information in an intelligible form.

(l) obtain information without any discrimination.

(m) obtain information at an affordable cost.

(n) obtain information relating to corruption.

(o) obtain information relating to the life and liberty of a person.

(p) obtain information relating to any action taken by a public authority in denying the right conferred under this Act.

The Sikkim Co-operative Societies Act, 1961

[Received the assent of the Governor on the 1st day of March, 1961; assent first published in the Sikkim Government Gazette, Extraordinary, dated the 1st day of March, 1961.]

An Act to provide for the registration of Co-operative Societies and to consolidate and amend the law relating to such Societies in the State of Sikkim.

Preamble

Whereas it is expedient to provide for the registration of Co-operative Societies and to consolidate and amend the law relating to such Societies in the State of Sikkim;

It is hereby enacted in the Twelfth Year of the Republic of India, as follows:-

Chapter I

PRELIMINARY

1. Short title, extent and commencement.

(1) This Act may be called the Sikkim Co-operative Societies Act, 1961.

(2) It extends to the whole of the State of Sikkim.

(3) It shall come into force on such date as the State Government may, by notification in the Sikkim Government Gazette, appoint.

2. Definitions.

In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires,-

(a) "Co-operative society" means a society registered under this Act;

(b) "Co-operative society with share capital" means a co-operative society which has been authorised to raise share capital;

(c) "Co-operative society without share capital" means a co-operative society which has not been authorised to raise share capital;

(d) "Registrar" means the Registrar of Co-operative Societies appointed under section 3;

(e) "prescribed" means prescribed by rules made under this Act;

(f) "State Government" means the Government of Sikkim.

3. Appointment of Registrar and Assistant Registrar.

(1) The State Government may, by notification in the Sikkim Government Gazette, appoint a person to be the Registrar of Co-operative Societies.

(2) The State Government may, by notification in the Sikkim Government Gazette, appoint such number of Assistant Registrars of Co-operative Societies as it thinks fit.

An Act to repeal the Tamil Nadu Essential Services Maintenance Act, 1980.

Be it enacted by the Legislature of the State of Tamil Nadu in the Fifty-seventh Year of the Republic of India as follows:—

1. Short title and commencement. - (1) This Act may be called the Tamil Nadu Essential Services Maintenance (Repeal) Act, 2006.

Explain the repeal of the law. What is the significance of the repeal?

The Tamil Nadu Essential Services Maintenance (Repeal) Act, 2006 repealed the Tamil Nadu Essential Services Maintenance Act, 1980. The Tamil Nadu Essential Services Maintenance Act, 1980 was enacted to provide for the maintenance of essential services in the State of Tamil Nadu. The repeal of the Act means that the provisions of the Act are no longer in force and have been replaced by the Tamil Nadu Essential Services Maintenance (Repeal) Act, 2006.

The significance of the repeal is that it removes the legal obligation to maintain essential services in Tamil Nadu and allows for the possibility of different laws being enacted in the future to regulate essential services. This could lead to changes in the regulation of essential services in Tamil Nadu, such as the introduction of new laws to ensure the provision of essential services or the repeal of other laws that regulate essential services.

A legal document is a document that evidences a legal or other binding agreement between two or more parties. These documents can be used to establish rights and obligations, as well as to protect the parties involved in the agreement. The most common types of legal documents are contracts, wills, trusts, and deeds.

### Contracts

A contract is an agreement between two or more parties that creates a legal obligation. The parties to a contract must have the capacity to enter into the agreement, and the agreement must be supported by consideration. Consideration is something of value that is given by one party to the other in exchange for the other party's performance.

### Wills

A will is a legal document that sets out a person's wishes regarding the distribution of their property after they die. A will can also appoint an executor to carry out the wishes of the deceased. Wills must be signed by the testator (the person making the will) and witnessed by two people who are not beneficiaries under the will.

### Trusts

A trust is a legal arrangement in which one person (the settlor) transfers property to another person (the trustee) to hold for the benefit of a third person (the beneficiary). The trustee is responsible for managing the property according to the terms of the trust agreement. Trusts can be used to avoid probate taxes and to protect assets from creditors.

### Deeds

A deed is a legal document that transfers ownership of property from one person to another. Deeds must be signed by both parties and witnessed by two people who are not beneficiaries under the deed.

An Act to provide for exemption from payment of court fees in certain cases in Sikkim and for matters connected therewith.

## The Sikkim Court Fees (Exemption and Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1983

WHEREAS the Sikkim Legislative Assembly has decided that it is expedient to provide for exemption from payment of court fees in certain cases in Sikkim and for matters connected therewith;

BE it enacted by the Sikkim Legislative Assembly in the Thirty-Fourth Year of the Republic of India as follows:-

## Short title, extent and commencement

1. (1) This Act may be called the Sikkim Court Fees (Exemption and Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1983.

(2) It extends to the whole of Sikkim.

(3) It shall come into force on such date as the Governor may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint.

## Exemption from court fees

2. ## 1985. The following Act of the Sikkim Legislative Assem bly having received the assent of the Governor on the 28th day of June, 1985, is hereby published for general information:-

THE SIKKIM CULTIVATORS' PROTECTION ACT, 1')85 (Ad No. 5 of 1985)

AN ACT to make provisions for protection of cultivators against termination of cultivation of lands cultivated by them, for restoration of such lands in case of termination of cultivation and for other matters connected therewith.

WHEREAS it is expedient to make provisions for the protection of cultivators against termination of cultivation of lands cultivated by them and for restoration of such lands in case of termination of cultivation and for other matters connected therewith;

BE it enacted by the Sikkim Legislative Assembly in the Thirty-first Year of the Republic of India as follows:-

1. Short title, extent and commencement.-

(1) This Act may be called the Sikkim Cultivators' Protection Act, 1985.

(2) It extends to the whole of Sikkim.

(3) It shall come into force on such date as the State Government may, by notification, appoint.

2. Definitions.-

In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires,-

(a) "Cultivator" means a person who cultivates land and includes the legal heir of such person; and

(b) "Cultivator's land" means any land cultivated by a cultivator.

3. Prohibition of termination of cultivation.-

(1) No land cultivated by a cultivator shall be terminated by any person without the permission of the landowner.

(2) The landowner may, after giving one month's notice in writing to the cultivator, terminate the cultivation of any land cultivated by him, if the cultivator fails to cultivate the land for two consecutive years.

4. Restoration of cultivator's land.-

(1) If the landowner terminates the cultivation of any land cultivated by a cultivator without the permission of the landowner, the cultivator shall have the right to cultivate such land on the same terms and conditions as were applicable to him before the termination of the cultivation.

(2) If the landowner terminates the cultivation of any land cultivated by a cultivator with the permission of the landowner, the cultivator shall have the right to cultivate such land on the same terms and conditions as were applicable to him before the termination of the cultivation

The Indian legal system is a common law system, which means that it is based on precedent and case law. This means that courts look to previous cases to determine how to interpret and apply the law in new situations. The Indian Constitution is the supreme law of the land, and it establishes the structure of the government and the rights and duties of citizens. The Constitution also guarantees certain fundamental rights, such as the right to life and personal liberty, the right to freedom of speech and expression, and the right to equality before the law.
